evidence: CVE.org API record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-61460 is PUBLISHED and identifies CWE-639: authenticated users can edit, update, or delete records owned by other users because record-level ownership validation is missing in LeadController, PersonController, OrganizationController, QuoteController, and ActivityController.

Vendor issue https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm/issues/2559 explains that route-name ACL is enforced by Webkul\Admin\Http\Middleware\Bouncer, while record ownership is an opt-in controller check via bouncer()->getAuthorizedUserIds(); direct object-id edit/update/destroy paths omit it.

At tag v2.2.3, LeadController edit/update/updateAttributes/updateStage/destroy resolve or mutate the requested id without preventUnauthorizedAccess; at v2.2.4 the vendor added preventUnauthorizedAccess before those sinks.

Remote first-party history shows multiple independently introduced vulnerable sinks across five controllers; for example 9cbd134a63b3317675972483dd8e60e6bf6f74c4 added the Lead view ownership restriction while existing Lead update/destroy sinks remained unrestricted, but this alone does not establish the smallest first-writer for the entire multi-controller advisory.

With GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1, git cat-file -e 9cbd134a63b3317675972483dd8e60e6bf6f74c4^{commit} reports missing in the assigned clone; the same clone's origin is https://github.com/HQ1995/vibe-security-radar.git, not the bundle repo.

GitHub identifies ddd4219f5327500e8e32d8ea2f29c47a4abdf670 as the parent of remote candidate 9cbd134a63b3317675972483dd8e60e6bf6f74c4, and the parent LeadController lacks the view ownership hunk, but neither object exists in the assigned clone and the exact atomic BIC remains unresolved.
The assigned clone lacks the target repository commit graph, so candidate merges, carriers, and finer public members cannot be exhaustively decomposed or excluded locally.

CVE.org records versions 0 through 2.2.3 as affected; git ls-remote maps vendor tag v2.2.3 to 6cda4f6297042d74769c38fcbc1b7ebe6df54ab6, and raw v2.2.3 LeadController source contains the unrestricted sinks, but ancestry and object membership cannot be verified in the assigned clone.

git ls-remote maps vendor tag v2.2.4 to 55b48fe86d7f196c32581ed80bb723cf0e18d44e; raw v2.2.4 source contains preventUnauthorizedAccess and its LeadController call sites, but the assigned clone cannot prove fix ancestry or release membership.

Vendor PR https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm/pull/2567 is merged and its first member cccc12df2c405f6c00633bff13d7befd8dd0ee4f directly adds ownership checks and authorized-record filtering across the affected controllers.
With GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1, git cat-file -e cccc12df2c405f6c00633bff13d7befd8dd0ee4f^{commit} reports missing in the assigned clone, so no direct_fix_sha can satisfy the output contract.
Atomic BIC identity is not closed and no target commit object is available locally; remote author names or later repository AI activity cannot support BIC-only attribution.

bug_semantics: Authenticated CRM routes enforce action-level ACL but do not automatically scope repository lookups by record owner. For users limited to individual or group visibility, attacker-controlled record ids therefore flow through edit/view-form, update, attribute/stage update, delete, and mass-action endpoints to unrestricted repository reads or mutations, exposing, reassigning, modifying, or deleting another user's records.
flaw_origin: The advisory spans independently evolved sinks in five controllers. Remote history supplies plausible first-writer boundaries for individual paths, including the Lead ownership-asymmetry commit, but the bundle binds to a non-target clone that lacks every target commit object; the smallest atomic BIC and its parent tree cannot be established under the required local-Git gate.

evidence: No atomic BIC commit object is present in the assigned clone, so BIC-local AI evidence cannot be inspected or ruled out.

Recording target SHAs would violate the commit-object gate, while inferring NOT_AI from remote author names would violate BIC-only attribution. The required result is therefore EVIDENCE_GAP.
